chief_complaint: fever, flank pain, nausea, and costovertebral tenderness
hpi_details: A 23-year-old male presents to the clinic with fever, flank pain, nausea, and costovertebral tenderness. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: He thinks he strained a deep muscle in his back while deadlifting at the gym and caught a stomach bug at the same time.
concerns: He is worried that he will fail his upcoming college finals if he has to be admitted to the hospital.
expectations: He hopes to get some strong pain pills and anti-nausea medicine so he can go back to his dorm to study.

investigation_events.title: Point-of-care urinalysis
investigation_events.availability_message: The point-of-care urinalysis is now available; the urine culture remains pending beyond this encounter.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Acute Pyelonephritis is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Acute Pyelonephritis: Oral Ciprofloxacin or IV Ceftriaxone depending on severity, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: fever, flank pain, nausea, and costovertebral tenderness

Key HPI features: A 23-year-old male presents to the clinic with fever, flank pain, nausea, and costovertebral tenderness. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals: Temp 38.9C, HR 108, BP 118/74. Right costovertebral angle tenderness on percussion. No peritoneal signs. Urinalysis: positive leukocyte esterase and nitrites, WBC 20-30/hpf, few bacteria; urine culture pending.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Acute Pyelonephritis.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Cystitis alone without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: High fever with rigors or signs of sepsis — may need IV antibiotics and admission.
management_principles: Obtain urinalysis and urine culture before starting antibiotics.
Select oral Ciprofloxacin for mild cases able to tolerate oral intake, or IV Ceftriaxone/broader coverage for patients with sepsis, vomiting, or inability to take oral therapy.
Reassess within 48-72 hours; escalate to admission if fever persists, sepsis develops, or there is evidence of obstruction.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) Clinical Practice Guidelines

reference_soap.subjective: 23M with fever, flank pain, nausea, and generalized fatigue, gradually worsening, consistent with an ascending urinary tract infection.
reference_soap.objective: T 38.9C, HR 108, BP 118/74. Right costovertebral angle tenderness on percussion. No peritoneal signs. Urinalysis: positive leukocyte esterase and nitrites, WBC 20-30/hpf.
reference_soap.assessment: Acute Pyelonephritis, likely uncomplicated given no signs of sepsis or obstruction.
reference_soap.plan: Obtain urinalysis and urine culture before antibiotics, assess for sepsis or urinary obstruction, and determine whether admission/IV therapy is required. Select empiric antibiotics using local resistance patterns and culture results; if an oral fluoroquinolone is used where resistance is a concern, provide an appropriate initial parenteral dose according to local guidance. Seek urgent evaluation for sepsis, vomiting/inability to take oral therapy, obstruction, or failure to improve.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Acute Pyelonephritis
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Acute Pyelonephritis
Implement evidence-based management plan: Oral Ciprofloxacin or IV Ceftriaxone depending on severity

teaching.one_liner: A bacterial infection that has ascended from the bladder to the kidney, causing fever, flank pain, nausea, and costovertebral angle tenderness — more serious than simple cystitis.
red_flags: High fever with rigors or signs of sepsis — may need IV antibiotics and admission

must_ask.say: Where exactly is the pain — your back or side?
Have you had a fever or chills?
Any burning urination or frequency before this started?
Have you felt nauseated or vomited?
How long has this been going on?

history.answer: I came in because I have had a high fever and a bad ache in my right side for the past two days.
It began about two days ago with a mild fever and some burning when I peed, and both the fever and my right flank pain have gotten significantly worse since yesterday.
My thermometer showed 38.9 degrees Celsius this morning, and the fever has been staying high with severe shivering and shaking chills.
I took two tablets of acetaminophen about four hours ago, but my fever barely came down and went right back up.
No, I do not have any cough, phlegm, sore throat, or trouble breathing.
Yes, it stings and burns when I urinate, I have to go much more often than usual, and my urine looks cloudy.
It is a constant, throbbing deep ache in my right back and flank that feels much sharper whenever I move or bump that area.
I have felt quite nauseous since yesterday and have no appetite, but I have not thrown up or had any diarrhea.
I have a slight generalized headache from the high temperature, but my neck is not stiff and my thinking is completely clear.
No, I have not noticed any skin rashes, red spots, or bug bites with black crusts anywhere.
I wake up soaked in sweat when my fever breaks, but I have not had chronic night sweats or any weight loss.
No, I have not noticed or felt any swollen glands or lumps in my neck, armpits, or groin.
No, I have not traveled abroad, gone hiking in the woods, worked on a farm, or handled any animals recently.
No one at my home, school, or workplace has been sick with a fever or infection recently.
No, I have never received chemotherapy, and I do not take steroids or any medications that weaken the immune system.
No, I have never had any heart murmurs, valve problems, or congenital heart conditions, and I have not had any dental cleanings or procedures recently.
No, I have not started any new prescription medicines, herbal remedies, or over-the-counter supplements.
I am in a monogamous relationship, consistently use barrier protection, have no history of sexually transmitted infections, and have never injected drugs.
I have felt utterly exhausted and drained of energy since the fever spiked yesterday.
I thought maybe I pulled a deep lower back muscle doing deadlifts at the gym and caught a bad stomach bug on top of it.
I'm really worried that being stuck in the hospital will make me miss my college final exams this week.
I'm hoping to get some strong painkillers and something for the nausea so I can go rest in my dorm.
I have never been diagnosed with any chronic medical conditions like diabetes, high blood pressure, or kidney disease.
I have never had any operations and I have never been hospitalized.
I do not take any regular prescription medications, just the acetaminophen I took earlier today for the fever.
I have no known allergies to any antibiotics, pain relievers, or other medications.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any vaping or tobacco products.
I only drink occasionally in social settings, maybe a beer or two a month, and I have had nothing to drink recently.
I am a university student living in an apartment near campus.
There is no family history of kidney disorders, kidney stones, or serious chronic medical conditions.

exam.finding: Temperature 38.9 C, heart rate 108 beats per minute, blood pressure 118/74 mmHg, respiratory rate 18 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Pharynx is normal without erythema, exudates, or tonsillar swelling.
Both tympanic membranes are clear and translucent with normal light reflexes and no effusion.
No palpable cervical, submandibular, or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy.
Clear breath sounds heard bilaterally throughout all lung fields without wheezes, crackles, or rhonchi.
Tachycardic rate with regular rhythm; normal S1 and S2 without murmurs, gallops, or friction rubs.
Abdomen is soft, flat, and non-tender to light and deep palpation, with no guarding or rigidity.
Marked sharp tenderness elicited by gentle fist percussion over the right costovertebral angle; left side non-tender.
Liver edge and spleen tip are not palpable beneath the costal margins.
No cutaneous eruptions, petechiae, purpura, or tick-bite eschars identified.
Neck is completely supple with full passive flexion; negative Kernig and Brudzinski signs.
